title: Earthquakes
standard_code: Grade 7, Quarter 4: Earth and Space Science
standard_text: Earthquakes are caused by movement along faults; focus and epicenter; magnitude and intensity; the Philippines' active faults and trenches; earthquake hazards (ground shaking, liquefaction, landslides, tsunamis) and preparedness. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 7, Quarter 4: Earth and Space Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Earth and Space Science): faults, focus and epicenter, seismic waves, magnitude and intensity, Philippine faults, tsunamis and preparedness. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Earthquakes happen when rocks move suddenly along faults.
key_sub: Duck, Cover and Hold during an earthquake.
body_html:
How to think about it

An earthquake is the shaking of the ground when rocks along a fault move suddenly and release energy as seismic waves. The focus is where the rocks break underground; the epicenter is the point on the surface directly above it.

Magnitude measures the energy released; intensity describes the shaking and damage at a place. The Philippines has many active faults, such as the Philippine Fault Zone and the Valley Fault System, so PHIVOLCS monitors earthquakes and schools hold drills.

Example

What is the point on the surface above the focus?

Epi- means above

Answer: the epicenter

Example

The sea suddenly pulls back after a strong quake. What should you do?

Tsunami sign

Answer: go to high ground at once

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up magnitude and intensity.
  • Running outside while the ground is still shaking.
  • Thinking tsunamis only happen during typhoons.

faq.q: Why does the Philippines have many earthquakes?
faq.a: It lies where plates meet, on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

faq.q: What should be in a family earthquake plan?
faq.a: A meeting place, a go bag and knowing how to turn off gas and electricity.
